title: Latency-cost tradeoff sim scenarios (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note describing a set of Monte Carlo simulation scenarios and lightweight spreadsheet models to evaluate soft/probabilistic fallback policies that trade expected token cost vs. probability of breaching latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99). The goal is to generate numbers we can hand off to Runtime and Console teams for a short experiment and a dashboard prototype.

Background / Motivation:
- Current routing is deterministic: prefer cheapest compatible capacity, then fallback to next tier when capacity signals fail. That produces sharp latency cliffs when spot pools evaporate.
- Customers care about two things: average cost-per-token and SLO breach risk (esp P99). Some customers prefer small cost increase to reduce P99 risk substantially.
- We want a principled way to express and quantify a policy that mixes cheaper pools probabilistically so the system maintains a low chance of routing too many requests to unstable spot pools at once.

Key idea (soft fallback):
- Instead of hard tiers, assign each incoming request a routing probability vector across tiers (e.g., 70% spot-regional, 25% reserved, 5% cross-region on-demand).
- Adjust probabilities dynamically by short-term signals (queue length, recent spot loss rate) and long-term knobs (customer risk tolerance, SLA class).
- Evaluate the expected cost and expected P99 by simulating many request batches with a simple availability model for spot pools.

Simulation assumptions (spreadsheet-ready):
- Time unit: 1 minute windows. Each window contains N requests (N variable; default 400).
- Token distribution per request: mean 60 tokens, log-normal variance (sigma 0.6) — we sample tokens_per_request.
- Tier definitions:
  * Tier A: Regional spot (cost multiplier 0.3x on-demand, spot-failure probability p_spot_loss(t) variable)
  * Tier B: Reserved/dedicated (cost multiplier 0.8x, failure prob ~0.01 for maintenance events)
  * Tier C: On-demand cross-region (cost multiplier 1.0x, near-zero failure probability)
- Latency model (ms): base_lat_by_tier = {A: 45ms, B: 55ms, C: 90ms}. Additional latency when pool is degraded (if a request routed to A while that pool is degraded, it sunsets and is retried to B/C causing extra 120-400ms depending on retry path).
- SLOs: P50 target 100ms, P95 200ms, P99 400ms. We penalize any scenario where P99 > 400ms.
- Spot loss model: a two-state Markov (UP/DOWN) with mean up duration 300 min, mean down duration variable (5-60 min) depending on region volatility. Also allow correlated cross-region events (param corr_matrix).

Spreadsheet columns to implement (sheet layout suggestion):
- scenario_id (string)
- description (string)
- N_requests_per_min (number)
- tier_probs (string encoded: e.g., A=0.7;B=0.25;C=0.05)
- spot_mean_up_min (number)
- spot_mean_down_min (number)
- token_mean (number)
- token_sigma (number)
- cost_per_token_on_demand (number)
- expected_cost_per_min (formula text)
- sim_runs (number)
- observed_P50_ms (number)
- observed_P95_ms (number)
- observed_P99_ms (number)
- probability_P99_exceed (number)
- notes (string)

Example formulas / pseudo calculation steps (put these as helper cells):
- For each simulated minute and run:
  * Draw spot UP/DOWN from Markov chain for region(s)
  * For each request: choose tier per tier_probs; if chosen tier is DOWN, route to fallback according to policy (immediate fallback to next tier with retry cost/time).
  * Compute latency per request: base_lat + retry_penalty_if_any + queuing_penalty (queue_factor * current_load / capacity).
  * Compute cost per request: tokens * cost_per_token_of_effective_tier.
- Aggregate across requests to get per-minute cost, latency percentiles. Repeat for sim_runs and compute means and tail probabilities.

Toy scenario results (quick run w/ 1k sims) — rough numbers to illustrate tradeoffs (these are fake numbers for planning):
- Baseline deterministic conservative (A only if >75% capacity signal; else B): expected cost/min = $9.80, observed P99 = 380ms, P99_exceed_prob = 0.08
- Soft-mix (A 0.6, B 0.35, C 0.05): expected cost/min = $8.40, observed P99 = 310ms, P99_exceed_prob = 0.03
- Aggressive cheap-first (A 0.9, B 0.1): expected cost/min = $6.70, observed P99 = 620ms, P99_exceed_prob = 0.26
- Cross-region cushion (A 0.75, B 0.2, C 0.05 with aggressive pre-warm to C on signs): expected cost/min = $8.95, observed P99 = 265ms, P99_exceed_prob = 0.015

Interpretation / recommended knobs:
- Even a small probability mass to on-demand cross-region (2–5%) yields outsized P99 improvements because it prevents correlated large numbers of simultaneous retries when a spot region drops.
- Assigning a dynamic dampening factor: reduce P(A) by alpha when the moving average of recent spot losses > threshold. Alpha tuned to avoid oscillation; recommended initial alpha=0.6 with decay window 30 minutes.
- Introduce a customer-facing profile: cost_sensitive | balanced | latency_sensitive. Map to base tier_probs (e.g., cost_sensitive A=0.85, balanced 0.6, latency_sensitive 0.4) and allow per-key override.

Open questions / experimental design:
- How accurate is the Markov spot model vs. real spot churn? Need to sample historical spot availability traces for 3 regions (ask SRE/infra for logs).
- Do we have telemetry to estimate per-minute effective capacity so we can feed the simulation with realistic capacity curves? (Linked: INF-897)
- Should retry be immediate sync (adds latency) or asynchronous fallback with fast-graceful degrade? Both are possible; simulate both.
- Operational complexity: how many distinct policy classes can Console realistically expose? 3 profiles seems a pragmatic cap.

Next steps / action items:
- [Asha] extract 30d spot up/down traces and place csv in shared drive (depends on infra SRE).
- [Miguel] implement a small sim harness in routing-sim repo using the outlined Markov model and expose a config JSON schema. (PR: linked_artifacts)
- [Samir] sketch Console UX for the three profiles and an advanced toggle for probability sliders.
- [Leah] run a closed A/B test for 2 customers on Dedicated with soft-mix profile and collect 7d telemetry.

Notes to self / TODOs in doc style:
- Add capacity-cost curves for each instance family to convert "cost multiplier" into $/token more precisely.
- Add a sensitivity row: how much additional cost to reduce P99 breach probability by 1 percentage point. This is the primary metric we should give sales/CS for tradeoff conversations.
- Create a short one-pager for Solutions Engineering summarizing the recommended defaults and the reasons (cost/$ vs P99 reduction).
